Megafone

A battery-powered portable loudspeaker used by crew to issue commands and instructions during evacuation or inoperative PA conditions.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Megafone?

In this glossary, Megafone refers to: A battery-powered portable loudspeaker used by crew to issue commands and instructions during evacuation or inoperative PA conditions.

How is Megafone used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Sistema PA inoperante; tripulação utilizou megafone para orientar passageiros durante evacuação de emergência; todas instruções repassadas claramente."

Why does Megafone matter in aviation?

Megafone matters because it supports clear communication in Cabin Safety contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Megafone?

Megafone is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Megafone belong to?

In this glossary, Megafone is grouped under Cabin Safety. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

A battery-powered portable loudspeaker used by crew to issue commands and instructions during evacuation or inoperative PA conditions.

Operational example

PA system was inoperative; crew used megaphone to direct passengers during emergency evacuation; all instructions relayed clearly.

Localized term

Megafone

Localized example
